source.title: Feature Dynamics as Implicit Data Augmentation: A Depth-Decomposed View on Deep Neural Network Generalization
source.authors: Tian-Yu Ruan; Kuo Gai; Shi-Hua Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests temporal consistency under randomized and corrupted labels and reports that it collapses when semantic label structure is damaged. It does not test whether the networks fit random labels to zero training error; its evidence refines the generalization claim through a different behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper reports no result measuring training error, test error, or training time on completely random labels. Its relevant result is temporal consistency under 40% randomized labels. SGD-noise covariance, feature composites, and the reported results for other interventions do not directly measure versions V1–V6.
record.test_reason: The study measures agreement between networks assembled from different training checkpoints under clean versus 40% randomized labels. This temporal-consistency measure does not establish random-label fitting, optimization speed, noise-dependent training/test error, regularization effects, or whether real-label patterns are learned before noise. Its own results therefore test none of V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record largely captures the authors' interpretation, but 'heavily corrupted supervision' overstates the demonstrated label conditions: the reported comparison uses 40% randomized labels. The authors argue that temporal consistency reflects structured feature augmentation supporting generalization, persists on unseen and corrupted inputs with clean supervision, and breaks down under randomized supervision.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies temporal consistency of composite networks made from different training checkpoints, not the original random-label memorization intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Consistency depends on label condition: it remains concentrated near 1.0 with clean labels and collapses with 40% randomized labels. The paper also describes test-set and corruption settings, but these do not measure fitting random labels.

fits_no_version.finding: With 40% randomized training labels, ResNet-20 checkpoint-composite consistency shifts away from 1.0 on CIFAR-10 test data and CIFAR-10C; clean-label consistency remains concentrated near 1.0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temporal agreement between composite and reference networks depends on semantic structure in training supervision, including when evaluated on unseen or corrupted inputs.

record.problems: The relevant randomized-label evidence measures temporal consistency, not training error, test error, or the sequence in which labels are learned. The noisy-label condition reported for the main comparison is 40%; no full corruption sweep is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Other reported results concern clean-label temporal consistency, test/corruption generalization, feature dynamics, or interventions that do not measure V1–V6.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error and chance test error on completely random labels with unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative fitting time for true and random labels, and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs. Corrupted test inputs do not establish fitting unstructured training inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error across a label-corruption sweep.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting, and whether removing regularization impairs true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-label patterns before memorizing noise. Checkpoint-composite agreement does not measure that learning order.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T5 classification conflicts with its correctly unlinked rows. A significant change in temporal consistency does not qualify or contradict the listed random-label memorization claims.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks reach zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels, have test error at chance, and do so without changes to architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence speed for true versus random labels or different corruption fractions.
Whether the networks fit shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training-set fit and test error across a sweep from clean to fully randomized labels; the paper reports temporal consistency for clean and 40%-randomized labels only.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on fitting random labels and generalization on true labels.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training, or whether real and random labels are learned differently in the sense tested by Arpit et al. (2017).

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Measured consistency between composite and reference networks under clean labels and 40% randomized training labels.
rows.measure: Distribution of temporal consistency between composite and reference networks
rows.baseline: Clean-label consistency distribution remains sharply concentrated near 1.0
rows.value: With 40% randomized training labels, the consistency distribution collapses: long tails emerge and mass shifts away from 1.0.
rows.uncertainty: Welch’s t-test p-values: Depth 1 5.46244 × 10−06; Depth 2 2.02578 × 10−14; Depth 3 5.46244 × 10−06
rows.note: This is a consistency result, not a measurement of fitting random labels or the training/test error described by V1.
rows.check: The reported consistency collapse is observed, but cannot determine any claim version's effect. Specify CIFAR-10 test data for Figure 7(b). Appendix E reports representative depth-wise p-values without identifying their evaluation dataset, so their attribution specifically to this row is unverified.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Measured consistency between composite and reference networks under clean labels and 40% randomized training labels.
rows.measure: Distribution of temporal consistency between composite and reference networks
rows.baseline: With clean labels, consistency distributions remain sharply concentrated near 1.0.
rows.value: With 40% randomized training labels, the consistency distribution collapses: long tails emerge and mass shifts away from 1.0.
rows.uncertainty: Welch’s t-test p-values are reported for representative clean versus noisy-label comparisons, but the text does not map them to this specific condition.
rows.note: This measures consistency under corrupted inputs, not the training/test errors in V1 or V4.
rows.check: The reported consistency collapse is observed, but cannot determine any claim version's effect. Figure 7(d) supports the Gaussian-blur condition; Appendix Figure 17 covers multiple corruption types and should not be treated as exclusively Gaussian blur.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
